news.headline: India, Canada explore energy partnership as both sides push to seal trade deal
news.story_lead: India, Canada explore energy partnership as both sides push to seal trade deal Negotiators will meet in New Delhi early next month for the sixth round of CEPA talks, with both countries aiming to finalise the agreement. India and Canada may explore deeper energy cooperation while expeditiously concluding negotiations for a comprehensive free trade deal, people aware of the matter said, adding that the countries plan to establish a two-way energy supply chain in which India would import Canadian oil and gas and send refined petroleum products the other way. A team of Canadian negotiators will visit New Delhi early next month to participate in the sixth round of free trade talks, they said, requesting anonymity.
news.full_article_text: India, Canada explore energy partnership as both sides push to seal trade deal Negotiators will meet in New Delhi early next month for the sixth round of CEPA talks, with both countries aiming to finalise the agreement. India and Canada may explore deeper energy cooperation while expeditiously concluding negotiations for a comprehensive free trade deal, people aware of the matter said, adding that the countries plan to establish a two-way energy supply chain in which India would import Canadian oil and gas and send refined petroleum products the other way. A team of Canadian negotiators will visit New Delhi early next month to participate in the sixth round of free trade talks, they said, requesting anonymity. Both sides are making efforts to conclude negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) before an expected visit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Canada in mid-December, they added. The prime ministers of the two countries have decided to cooperate in key areas such as trade, energy , technology, security and people-to-people ties, they said. Deep Dive The High Commission of India in Ottawa last week announced Modi’s visit to Canada on December 11-12. Establishing a robust energy supply chain is one of the potential areas of cooperation, the people mentioned above said. Canadian oil sands are the world’s fourth largest oil deposits and it is also the fourth largest producer of crude oil in the world after the US, Russia and Saudi Arabia. It is also fifth largest producer of natural gas. While Canada is one of the top oil and gas producers, India is the world’s third biggest crude oil consumer after the US and China. It is also the second largest consumer of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG or cooking gas) and fourth largest consumer of liquefied natural gas (LNG). “India and Canada are in talks to establish reliable supply chains in key sectors such as crude oil, LPG, LNG, potash, nuclear fuel (uranium) and refined petroleum products. India is a major refining hub and it can ensure supply of fuels and petroleum products to Canada,” one of the people cited above said. Canada, which is one of the top energy producers in the world, requires refined products in huge quantities because of geographical issues (leading to logistical hurdles) and technical reasons (such as refinery configuration). Most refineries in Canada are not configured to process heavy and bituminous crude extracted from oil sands in Alberta. But some of the Indian refineries can process any type of crude, the people said. This was followed by Carney’s India visit in February-March this year. It was followed by India visits by Canadian foreign minister Anita Anand and trade minister Maninder Sidhu in mid-October. Sidhu was accompanied by a 300-strong Canadian business delegate, the largest Canadian trade delegation to India in 30 years. The people said that the negotiations for the India-Canada CEPA is progressing fast, and most of the key issues related to the free trade agreement have been resolved. Both sides are working to finalise the trade deal before December, aiming to raise two-way trade to Canadian $70 billion (US$50.4 billion) by 2030. Bilateral goods and services trade between India and Canada in 2025 was Canadian $30.4 billion (US$21.9 billion), with merchandise trade contributing Canadian $13.6 billion (US$9.8 billion). news.full_article_text: 30% of India’s croplands technically suitable for solar agrovoltaics: Pralhad Joshi Joshi also said the new PM-Kusum 2.0 includes a dedicated agrivoltaics component, with immense potential to expand India’s solar capacity while substantially benefiting farmers. An estimated 47.5 million hectares, or approximately 30%, of India’s 160 million hectares of cropland should be technically suitable for agrivoltaics—where solar panels are installed directly above existing farms, Union minister for new and renewable energy (MNRE) Pralhad Joshi said on Wednesday at the inauguration of the 7th edition of the AgriVoltaics World Conference (AWC) 2026 in Delhi’s Bharat Mandapam. “The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI) has estimated 47.5 million hectares, or approximately 30% of India’s 160 million hectares of cropland, is technically suitable for agrivoltaics. One deployment scenario covering 16 million hectares estimates annual electricity generation of 12,775 TWh, potentially comparable to or exceeding India’s projected electricity demand of 5,250–10,020 TWh by 2050,” said Joshi, stating one of the world’s most ambitious agrivoltaic programmes would be launched under the next phase of PM-Kusum. “Elevated and tilted structures could make agrivoltaic plants 25–30% more expensive than conventional ground-mounted solar installations, and the government aims to bridge this cost gap by supporting AgriPV capacity creation,” the minister added. The conference was inaugurated alongside the agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan too, who said any AgriPV policy must be designed to meet the practical requirements of India’s small and marginal farmers, who constitute more than 85% of the farming community. Currently, coverage of ground-mounted solar panels is part of the existing PM Kusum scheme, which provides subsidies to farmers for both ground-mounted panels and solar pumps. “The average landholding in the country is only 0.96 hectares. Thus, agrivoltaics models must allow farmers to continue cultivation instead of replacing farming with solar power generation,” Chouhan said. The conference also saw the launch of a Decision-Making Tool developed by the India Agrivoltaics Alliance (IAA) – which allows farmers to assess the AgriPV potential of their land and the cost required for installation. An AgriPV policy handbook was also launched, which officials said should provide a base for further deliberations on the final policy. “The three-day conference will allow suggestions and further ideas to be incorporated into the final policy planned,” a senior official said. Gandhiok has covered some recent events around the Capital too, ranging from the farmers' protests, the northeast Delhi riots and the CAA-NRC protests, reporting from the ground on all of these. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. news.headline: Parliament’s Central, Library halls gear up to host 12th BRICS forum next week
news.story_lead: Parliament’s Central, Library halls gear up to host 12th BRICS forum next week The event will discuss key issues such as ethical digital transformation, global governance reform and parliamentary diplomacy and feature cultural snapshots from different states and local cuisine. Two iconic parts of the Parliament complex—the Central Hall and the Library Hall (formerly the Chamber of Princes)—are being decked up to host the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum next week, officials said. The event will discuss key issues such as ethical digital transformation, global governance reform and parliamentary diplomacy and feature cultural snapshots from different states and local cuisine.
news.full_article_text: Parliament’s Central, Library halls gear up to host 12th BRICS forum next week The event will discuss key issues such as ethical digital transformation, global governance reform and parliamentary diplomacy and feature cultural snapshots from different states and local cuisine. Two iconic parts of the Parliament complex—the Central Hall and the Library Hall (formerly the Chamber of Princes)—are being decked up to host the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum next week, officials said. The event will discuss key issues such as ethical digital transformation, global governance reform and parliamentary diplomacy and feature cultural snapshots from different states and local cuisine. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has planned various programmes and a Culture Bazar in the Parliament complex. Craftsmen and artisans from different states, including Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, will display their works for the BRICS’ guests, according to an official. “Banquets would be hosted by Birla and Vice President CP Radhakrishnan, and guests will be given guided tours of the Parliament complex, New Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur,” a senior official told HT. The Central Hall will be the venue of the forum on October 26 and 27. The Library Hall of the Chamber of Princes, which was used as a reading room for MPs, would be used for an international event for the first time. “After Parliament shifted to the new building, the Library Hall lost its purpose. Now it is being refurbished for the BRICS Speakers’ Summit,” said a second official. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will attend the event for an interaction with delegates. Eleven countries, including India, China, Russia and Brazil, are members of the BRICS. Another 10 countries, including Belarus, Malaysia and Uzbekistan, are partners of this global alliance. A senior official said that all 21 countries are expected to attend the event. Speaker Birla will chair the inaugural session and also deliver the valedictory speech. His office has also lined up bilateral meetings between Birla and his counterparts. Union ministers, MPs, state-level presiding officers and global parliamentary leaders are also set to attend the programme. The themes centre around “Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development, featuring high-level sessions on institutional resilience, ethical AI/digital transformation, global governance reform, sustainability, parliamentary diplomacy, and capacity-building. The forum is expected to adopt a joint declaration covering all these issues. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Saubhadra Chatterji Saubhadra Chatterji is Deputy Political Editor at the Hindustan Times. He writes on both politics and policies.

Strategic experts highlight that despite Indonesia's participation in the pact alongside Pakistan and Turkiye, New Delhi's ongoing missile and defense cooperation with Jakarta will remain intact.
news.full_article_text:
### Signing of the Four-Nation 'Badr MoU'
In a notable security development, four nations—Pakistan, Turkiye, Qatar, and Indonesia—have formally signed a defense agreement titled the 'Badr MoU'. The pact brings together key countries from South Asia, West Asia, and Southeast Asia to deepen security and defense ties.

### Impact on India-Indonesia Bilateral Security Ties
The signing generated discussion regarding its potential impact on India's strategic relations with Indonesia, particularly given the inclusion of Pakistan and Turkiye in the pact. However, defense and strategic analysts have pointed out that the 'Badr MoU' will not derail or undermine missile cooperation and defense partnerships between New Delhi and Jakarta.

### Strategic Context for New Delhi
India maintains a strong strategic engagement with Indonesia under its Act East Policy and broader Indo-Pacific vision. Jakarta's pursuit of multi-alignment in foreign policy allows it to pursue regional defense arrangements while simultaneously advancing core strategic partnerships, including defense material and missile technology engagements with India.

hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### चार देशों के 'बद्र एमओयू' पर हस्ताक्षर
एक महत्वपूर्ण सुरक्षा घटनाक्रम में, चार देशों—पाकिस्तान, तुर्की, कतर और इंडोनेशिया—ने 'बद्र एमओयू' नामक एक रक्षा समझौते पर औपचारिक रूप से हस्ताक्षर किए हैं। यह समझौता दक्षिण एशिया, पश्चिम एशिया और दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया के प्रमुख देशों को रक्षा सहयोग बढ़ाने के लिए एक मंच पर लाता है।

### भारत-इंडोनेशिया द्विपक्षीय सुरक्षा संबंधों पर प्रभाव
इस समझौते में पाकिस्तान और तुर्की की उपस्थिति के कारण नई दिल्ली और जकार्ता के बीच रणनीतिक संबंधों पर पड़ने वाले प्रभाव को लेकर चर्चा शुरू हुई। हालांकि, रक्षा और रणनीतिक विश्लेषकों ने स्पष्ट किया है कि 'बद्र एमओयू' भारत और इंडोनेशिया के बीच मिसाइल सहयोग और रक्षा साझेदारी को प्रभावित नहीं करेगा।

### नई दिल्ली के लिए रणनीतिक संदर्भ

news.headline: Pope does not need further treatment after lung cancer surgery
news.story_lead: Pope Leo returned to St Peter's Square on Wednesday for his weekly general audience - Published 1 hour ago Pope Leo XIV does not need any further treatment following an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung, his doctors have said. Test results on tissue removed during surgery confirmed he had had a lung adenocarcinoma, as was initially diagnosed, and that the disease was localised, according to a statement shared by the Vatican. "A subsequent oncological assessment has confirmed that no further treatment is necessary," it added.
news.full_article_text: Pope Leo returned to St Peter's Square on Wednesday for his weekly general audience - Published 1 hour ago Pope Leo XIV does not need any further treatment following an operation to remove a cancerous growth from his lung, his doctors have said. Test results on tissue removed during surgery confirmed he had had a lung adenocarcinoma, as was initially diagnosed, and that the disease was localised, according to a statement shared by the Vatican. "A subsequent oncological assessment has confirmed that no further treatment is necessary," it added. The 71-year-old was discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital over the weekend four days after his operation - stopping to speak to well-wishers as he left the grounds. It comes as he held his first weekly general audience since leaving hospital at St Peter's Square on Wednesday. The surgery, which took place on 13 October and lasted for 90 minutes, included the removal of the lower lobe of the Pope's right lung. The pontiff himself had announced during his weekly Sunday prayers that he would be having the procedure - telling those gathered in St Peter's Square that doctors had found a nodule on his lung. He said at the time that it had been caught "at an early stage". Images shared days after his operation, on Friday, showed the Pope celebrating Mass from the hospital wearing green vestments and standing behind a makeshift altar. On the same day, the Vatican said he spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin over the phone to urge a ceasefire in the blockaded Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky to allow the delivery of food aid, and to call for "dialogue and peace". The pontiff had a similar phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday. Those close to the Pope have also previously said he was keen not to delay a trip to Latin America which is planned for early November. Related topics

news.headline: Jeweller who crafted 'Sengol' installed in Parliament dies at 99. PM Modi condoles loss
news.story_lead: Jeweller who crafted 'Sengol' installed in Parliament dies at 99. PM Modi condoles loss Ethiraj was the patriarch of the Vummidi family that owns 125-year-old Vummidi Bangaru Jewellers. India's leading jeweller Vummidi Ethiraj passed away in Chennai, on Wednesday at the age of 99.
news.full_article_text: Jeweller who crafted 'Sengol' installed in Parliament dies at 99. PM Modi condoles loss Ethiraj was the patriarch of the Vummidi family that owns 125-year-old Vummidi Bangaru Jewellers. India's leading jeweller Vummidi Ethiraj passed away in Chennai, on Wednesday at the age of 99. Following his demise, Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed deep sadness and condoled his death. PM Modi paid tribute to Ethiraj in a post on X, noting that he will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the Sengol that was presented to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. The PM said, "Deeply saddened by the passing of Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji. Hailing from a distinguished family based in Tamil Nadu, he will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the historic Sengol that was presented to Former Prime Minister Nehru." PM Modi said that many years later, in 2023, it was this government which had the honour of giving the 'Sengol' a place of pride in the new Parliament building. "Many years later, in 2023, it was our Government which had the honour of giving the Sengol a place of pride in the new Parliament building. During that time, I had the honour of meeting Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji and expressing gratitude for what he has done for our nation and culture. His life and craftsmanship represent a remarkable connection between India's glorious traditions and our national journey. My heartfelt condolences to his family and admirers. Om Shanti," the prime minister added. Also Read | Murugan’s resignation letter: Praise for Modi’s Tamil outreach, from Sitharaman and Jaishankar to Thirukkural and Sengol Condoling the death in a post on X, Vice President Radhakrishnan said he was "deeply saddened" by the demise of Ethiraj, "whose efforts in crafting the historic Sengol, a sacred symbol of India’s civilisational heritage, will always be remembered with respect and gratitude." "His invaluable contribution to preserving India’s rich tradition of jewellery craftsmanship leaves behind an enduring legacy. My heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones," he added. Also Read | What is ‘Sengol’, whose installation in new Parliament triggered row? Who was Vummidi Ethiraj? Ethiraj was the patriarch of the Vummidi family that owns the 125-year-old Vummidi Bangaru Jewellers, according to news agency PTI . Ethiraj worked on the creation of Sengol, the gold-plated silver sceptre, symbolising the handover of power from British authorities to independent India in 1947. On the eve of Independence, Nehru received the Sengol from the Adheenams (priests) of the Thiruvaduthurai Adheenam (Mutt) in Tamil Nadu, who travelled specially for the occasion, the report added. Decades later, the Sengol found a place of prominence in the new Parliament building. Crafted by Vummidi Jewellers, the Sengol was ceremonially installed in the new Parliament building by Prime Minister Modi on May 28, 2023. news.story_lead: 'Don't meddle with powers of other agencies': Supreme Court to ED in case against Pinarayi Vijayan In a special sitting held during the Dussehra break, the Supreme Court allowed Vijayan and others to appeal against the single judge’s October 9 order. The Supreme Court on Wednesday stayed the investigation against former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter and son-in-law, among others, in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case. It also reprimanded the Enforcement Directorate (ED), directing it to stay within its statutory limits and not meddle with powers of other agencies.
news.full_article_text: 'Don't meddle with powers of other agencies': Supreme Court to ED in case against Pinarayi Vijayan In a special sitting held during the Dussehra break, the Supreme Court allowed Vijayan and others to appeal against the single judge’s October 9 order. The Supreme Court on Wednesday stayed the investigation against former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter and son-in-law, among others, in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case. It also reprimanded the Enforcement Directorate (ED), directing it to stay within its statutory limits and not meddle with powers of other agencies. “You (ED) have done your statutory duty. It is for the state to do its statutory duty. You have got a scheduled offence; you file a complaint and go ahead with your prosecution. Don’t extend your hands beyond the statutory limits. We are making it very clear. Don’t use your power to meddle with the statutory powers of other investigation agencies,” Justice Bagchi remarked when the ED defended the high court’s order. The top court stayed further investigation for seven days , allowing the petitioners to pursue their appeals against the Kerala High Court’s order directing the registration of a criminal case. Deep Dive In a special sitting held during the week-long Dussehra break, the Supreme Court allowed Vijayan and others to appeal against the single judge’s October 9 order. The court set aside the Kerala High Court division bench’s October 15 decision dismissing their appeal. The state had registered a first information report (FIR) on October 12 and was proceeding with the investigation. Also Read: HC order to file FIR passed without hearing me: Pinarayi Vijayan tells SC A bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said, “We direct the investigation in the FIR shall remain stayed for a week. Our order shall not be taken as an opinion expressed on the interim relief that the division bench (of the high court) shall fashion based on facts and the law.” The court clarified that the registration of the FIR had not been stayed; only further investigation had been halted. The high court had relied on a communication sent by the ED to the state police on September 22, disclosing a cognisable offence in the CMRL-Exalogic case. It was alleged that the state-owned CMRL paid more than ₹ 2.78 crore to Exalogic Solutions Pvt Ltd, a company wholly owned by Vijayan’s daughter, Veena T, without receiving any services in return. The payments were made by CMRL to Exalogic between 2017 and 2020. In January 2017, CMRL engaged Veena as an IT and marketing consultant on a retainership basis. However, tax assessments for the period from 2013-14 to 2019-20, submitted by CMRL, reportedly revealed additional payments to Exalogic for which no services had been rendered. Vijayan, represented by senior advocates Siddharth Luthra and N. Hariharan, submitted that the dismissal of his appeal had left him without an effective remedy. They argued that even the October 9 order directing the registration of an FIR and further investigation had been passed without hearing Vijayan. Luthra informed the court that, following the registration of the fresh FIR, the ED had filed a fresh Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR), alleging money laundering arising from the same set of allegations. In this connection, Vijayan had also been summoned by the ED for questioning on October 23. The bench observed, “Howsoever high you will be, you cannot be above law. We will not order a stay on the FIR. But on the points of whether cognisable offence is made out, the statutory requirement of continuation of investigation, we have said that you need to be heard by the high court.” The court left the ED’s proceedings untouched, stating, “We express no opinion on the validity of the fresh ECIR and leave it open to be agitated in an independent proceeding (by the petitioner).” The state’s actions also came under scrutiny, as the bench noted that the FIR had been registered on the basis of information shared by the ED rather than on the state’s own initiative. It referred to the statutory safeguards under the Prevention of Corruption Act, particularly Section 17A, which requires prior approval from the competent authority before an investigation can proceed against a public servant in circumstances covered by the provision. The Kerala government, represented by senior standing counsel Ramesh Babu, submitted that the information provided by the ED disclosed a cognisable offence, a finding also made in the single judge’s order. The bench said, “It needs to be ascertained whether information received from ED under section 66(2) is a mandate. The single judge goes flip-flop on this issue. We want the division bench to apply its mind.” Vijayan’s lawyers also argued that the high court had erred in entertaining a petition filed by advocate K. M. Shajahan, an outsider to the proceedings. The attack came amid a new diplomatic push led by Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Witkoff met Russia's President Vladimir Putin in the city of St Petersburg on Wednesday - a day after meeting Ukraine's leader. Three-way talks were paused in February, after which Russia stepped up attacks as Ukraine ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles. Speaking on Wednesday, Trump said: "The other day I was talking to Vladimir Putin about settling his war with Ukraine, which I think we're getting closer to, by the way, maybe now the closest we've been." The US president has so far failed to bring the Russia-Ukraine war to an end despite his repeated comments that he would be able to achieve this. - Rosenberg: US diplomatic push offers little hope for imminent Ukraine peace Published 1 hour ago Trump's special envoy Witkoff went to St Petersburg after meeting Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky as well as the leaders of Norway and Finland in the Norwegian capital, Oslo, on Tuesday. It is not clear what specific proposals Witkoff brought to Putin, but Zelensky said after the talks that "strong" security guarantees for Ukraine and energy ceasefire proposals had been discussed. Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov said their ideas were not very "useful". Top officials from Russia, Ukraine and the US have held several rounds of talks aimed at ending the war. Russia blamed last month's "massive" Ukrainian strikes during its general elections for their disruption. Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory. The latest talks between Putin (right) and Witkoff lasted about three hours in St Petersburg Speaking to reporters after Wednesday's talks in St Petersburg, Ushakov suggested that a new round could be held around 10 November in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates. He stressed that the talks must focus on "building a security system for Russia and Ukraine after the end of the conflict." Ushakov also told reporters that Putin reiterated to Witkoff that Russian troops were advancing everywhere across the vast front line and had a "strategic initiative". Ukraine and its European allies have disputed Putin's claim, pointing to a virtual stalemate on the front. On Wednesday, Zelensky said he would accept a deal that would freeze the war along the current front line. "We call it 'ceasefire' or 'stop killings' like President Trump called it. Freeze and stop. And of course this is minimum what we need from Russia today," he told Fox News, adding that security guarantees for Ukraine could be discussed after this. Watch: Zelensky says US military intelligence sharing "works now" Witkoff described the latest talks as "constructive", while Kushner, who was participating via a video link, said: "There is still hard work ahead, but we have a real opportunity to move beyond this war and build a framework for lasting peace, security, and prosperity for generations to come." The talks were held amid a growing row between Ukraine and the US. Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president, and most recently "for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine". He has blamed Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries for fuel prices which have been rising since the start of the US-led war on Iran. He was also heavily criticised by Democratic and some Republican lawmakers after lifting sanctions on Russia - allowing it to release tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace". That was despite signing legislation to authorise fresh US sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas just weeks earlier. Zelensky - and Ukraine's European allies - criticised Trump's move. Last week, Kyiv accused Washington of withholding critical intelligence to warn Ukrainians about incoming Russian ballistic missile launches, resulting in many civilian deaths. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday rejected such accusations as "scandalous", and Zelensky said after the Oslo talks that intelligence sharing "works now" . Ukraine's military has also complained of speed restrictions to the US satellite internet network Starlink, which constricted its ability to use drones to conduct strikes against Russia. US officials have denied having requested such a slowdown and a bipartisan group of US senators has called for an urgent investigation . Hubbard had been in jail in Russia for allegedly fighting for Ukraine Before the Putin-Witkoff talks started, Russia released Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American citizen who had been given a jail sentence of nearly seven years for allegedly fighting on behalf of Ukraine. Trump said the former teacher was "on his way back home" and "there was no 'swap' necessary", while Witkoff called Putin a "humanitarian" for agreeing the release. When asked by a BBC reporter whether he agreed with such a description of the Kremlin leader, US Vice-President JD Vance said: "I agree with Steve Witkoff saying something nice to a person who just released an American hostage.
